name: CFTC
description: Commitments of Traders: weekly futures and options positioning by trader category - speculators, hedgers, managed money, dealers, leveraged funds, index traders - for every reportable US futures market, from the CFTC.

tools.name: Disaggregated report, futures and options combined
tools.description: The disaggregated split with options included. Prefer it for crude, natural gas and gold, where a large share of managed-money exposure is held through options and the futures-only figure understates it.

options.about: CFTC contract market code, `088691` for COMEX gold. The stable id for a market across weeks and report types - names get edited, codes do not. Exact match.
options.name: cftc_contract_market_code

options.about: Market and exchange as the report prints them, `GOLD - COMMODITY EXCHANGE INC.`. Exact match, upper case; use `$where` with `upper()` or `like` for anything looser.
options.name: market_and_exchange_names

options.about: Commodity name, `GOLD` or `CRUDE OIL`. Exact match, upper case. One commodity can span several markets.
options.name: commodity_name

options.about: Exchange code: `CBT`, `CME`, `NYME`, `CMX`, `ICUS`, `ICEU`. Exact match, and unreliable on its own: a quarter of the rows store the code with trailing spaces (`CMX ` beside `CMX`, the latest gold row among them), and equality on `CMX` misses every one of those. Filter on `cftc_contract_market_code` instead, or use `$where=cftc_market_code like 'CMX%'`.
options.name: cftc_market_code

options.about: Top-level commodity group: `AGRICULTURE`, `FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS` or `NATURAL RESOURCES`.
options.name: commodity_group_name

options.about: One report date, as `2026-08-25` or the full `2026-08-25T00:00:00.000`. Reports are as of Tuesday and published Friday. For a range use `$where`.
options.name: report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd

options.about: Report week label, `2026 Report Week 34`. Exact match.
options.name: yyyy_report_week_ww

options.about: A SoQL filter for anything the column filters cannot say: `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd > '2026-01-01' AND commodity_name = 'GOLD'`, `open_interest_all > 100000`, `market_and_exchange_names like '%CRUDE%'`. An unknown column answers HTTP 400 with the failing query echoed back.
options.name: $where

options.about: Sort, as `column ASC|DESC`, comma-separated for several. Defaults to `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd DESC` for ordinary row queries. With `$select`, no default order is added; supply an order compatible with the selected columns.
options.name: $order

options.about: Rows to return. The default is 1,000; the datasets hold hundreds of thousands, so a date or market filter is what keeps a page useful rather than this.
options.name: $limit

options.about: Rows to skip, for paging past `$limit`.
options.name: $offset

options.about: Columns to return, comma-separated, in place of all of them. `count(*)` on its own answers how many rows match. A selected subset no longer matches the declared fields, so read the declared list as what the full row carries.
options.name: $select

response.about: A bare array, one row per market and report date. Every value is a JSON string, numbers included - Socrata serialises numeric columns as decimal strings - and a column whose value is null is left out of the row rather than sent as null. An empty array means nothing matched; a filter on an unknown column answers HTTP 400 rather than an empty array. The same columns as disaggregated/futures-only with options folded in on a futures-equivalent basis.

fields.about: Row id: the report date as YYMMDD, the contract market code, and F for futures only or C for futures and options combined.
fields.name: id

fields.name: report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd

fields.about: Report week label, `2026 Report Week 34`.
fields.name: yyyy_report_week_ww

fields.about: The market on its own, `GOLD`.

response.about: A bare array, one row per market and report date. options.about: Exchange code: `CBT`, `CME`, `NYME`, `CMX`, `ICUS`, `ICEU`. options.about: A SoQL filter for anything the column filters cannot say: `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd > '2026-01-01' AND commodity_name = 'GOLD'`, `open_interest_all > 100000`, `market_and_exchange_names like '%CRUDE%'`. An unknown column answers HTTP 400 with the failing query echoed back.

options.about: Sort, as `column ASC|DESC`, comma-separated for several. Defaults to `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd DESC` for ordinary row queries. With `$select`, no default order is added; supply an order compatible with the selected columns.

options.about: Rows to return. The default is 1,000; the datasets hold hundreds of thousands, so a date or market filter is what keeps a page useful rather than this.

options.about: Rows to skip, for paging past `$limit`.

response.about: A bare array, one row per market and report date. Every value is a JSON string, numbers included - Socrata serialises numeric columns as decimal strings - and a column whose value is null is left out of the row rather than sent as null. An empty array means nothing matched; a filter on an unknown column answers HTTP 400 rather than an empty array. The same columns as legacy/futures-only, with options positions folded in on a futures-equivalent (delta-adjusted) basis. `futonly_or_combined` reads `Combined`.
